reviewed_by: Claude review of platform migrations and egress
reason: Four platform-layer defects. (1) SQLite Alembic migrations were not transactional: database.py hands a plain connection to Alembic and env.py only called context.begin_transaction(), but pysqlite never emits BEGIN before DDL, so create_table/create_index committed immediately while alembic_version moved only at the end; a data-dependent failure in 0011's backfill (a Finding whose asset_ids names a deleted Asset) left resource_relations behind and every later start failed with 'table resource_relations already exists'. env.py now sets isolation_level=None on the sqlite DBAPI connection, opens BEGIN IMMEDIATE before context.configure (Alembic then treats the transaction as external) and commits or rolls back itself; 0011 skips and logs dangling or cross-project legacy references instead of raising. (2) egress_helper._forward used an unconnected UDP socket and only compared the requester-chosen transaction id, so a worker sharing the namespace could forge the upstream answer and resolve() would install ACCEPT rules for arbitrary hosts; it now queries over a connected socket with a random private id, ignores datagrams that do not echo it, and maps the genuine reply back to the requester's id. (3) native_checkpoints.capture copied file by file while validating, leaving <workspace>/.agents/checkpoints/<uuid>/ with partial copies and no entity on rejection; it now validates every path and size first, copies into a .partial staging directory, renames on success and removes the staging directory (recording, not ignoring, removal errors) on failure. (4) cli export did not catch ExportError/NotFoundError and serve did not catch OSError from listener.bind, so operators saw raw tracebacks; both now print a bounded message to stderr and exit 1. Tests: test_sqlite_migration_failure_leaves_no_partial_schema_and_can_retry (a before_cursor_execute hook fails 0011 after its DDL; on main resource_relations survives the failure) and test_relation_migration_backfills_legacy_arrays_and_skips_dangling_ids (raises on main); test_policy_dns_forwarder_accepts_only_the_upstream_reply_with_its_own_id drives resolve() against a local UDP responder that first sends a forged reply from another socket and a wrong-id reply (on main the forged 8.8.4.4 answer gets the rule); test_checkpoint_capture_rejection_leaves_no_partial_files (on main the uuid directory with notes.md remains); test_export_reports_known_failures_without_tracebacks and test_serve_reports_a_busy_port_without_a_traceback use CliRunner (on main result.exception is NotFoundError / OSError instead of SystemExit). The rest of those four files plus test_session_projection_migration and test_terminal_history_migration cover the migration runner and Database bootstrap path that every NebulaStore now exercises through the transactional env.py.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change. No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:core-api (the real-Core journey suite matched through cli.py, database.py's migration runner and native_checkpoints.py) does not exercise a mid-migration failure, a forged DNS datagram inside the egress namespace, an oversized checkpoint file or a CLI export/bind error; the Python tests drive each of those directly. No full suites.
